Q: TypeScript error: PrismaClient expects constructor options when using generated client A:

The Prisma have removed the rust engine, so you need a driver adapter as they have mention
https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/setup-and-configuration/no-rust-engine

Change the client to have an adapter

import { PrismaPg } from '@prisma/adapter-pg'
import { PrismaClient } from '../generated/prisma/client'

const adapter = new PrismaPg({ connectionString: DATABASE_URL })
const prisma = new PrismaClient({ adapter })

Q: How to determine if a Selenium WebDriver is running in headless mode A:

I'm not crazy about this solution but it works.

from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By
from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC
from selenium.webdriver.support.wait import WebDriverWait

url = 'https://www.google.com'

options = webdriver.ChromeOptions()
options.add_argument('--headless=new')
driver = webdriver.Chrome(options=options)
driver.maximize_window()
driver.get(url)

print(f"headless: {any("headless" in option for option in options.arguments)}")
    
print(options.arguments) # this is just for verbose debugging purposes

This prints

headless: True
['--headless=new']

"headless" may not be unique enough based on whatever other options you are using. You might need to make it more specific or even the full string, "--headless=new".

I think the better way to do this is to handle it using configs. Have a config file that contains whether headless should be used or not. When you read in the config file, create a config object to store the config settings, and then check config.headless or whatever when you need to throughout your scripts.
